subject.title: [Feature]: Collapsible messages in Control UI chat

question: Should Control UI add inline collapse for long assistant Markdown, and what default threshold, latest-message behavior, and global-control policy should it use?
rationale: Current code already has adjacent side-reader, JSON, tool, and duplicate-message disclosure patterns, so automation should not choose a new default chat disclosure policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Bounded Inline Collapse
options.body: Implement a small first version that collapses older long assistant messages by line or height threshold, keeps the active or latest response readable, and leaves global controls for a follow-up unless maintainers want them now.

options.title: Prefer Existing Side Reader
options.body: Decline inline collapse for now and treat the canvas/sidebar reader plus truncated-history recovery as the supported long-message escape hatch.

options.title: Defer To Broader Chat UX
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for a broader chat readability and accessibility design before adding another disclosure state.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Inline Collapse
recommendation.body: Implement a small first version that collapses older long assistant messages by line or height threshold, keeps the active or latest response readable, and leaves global controls for a follow-up unless maintainers want them now.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-file blame and recent side-reader follow-up commits make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this UX policy choice.
